title: Trace ensemble and quantile stitching scrapbook
content:
Goal:
Short: build a repeatable, low-effort workflow to produce production-weighted p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency profiles and per-stage contribution breakdowns from mixed samples (synthetic + sampled prod traces).

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- We have many single-window trace audits but no compact, comparable report that stitches multiple sampling periods and synthetic runs into a single quantile-aware view.
- Need something that PMs and infra can read: big quantiles, what stage is the offender, and a prioritized mitigation list with expected tail impact.

Inputs we used for the first pass (source / sample details):
- Production sampled traces: 24h window (2025-01-07), trace sampling 1/1000 overall, increased to 1/100 for anomalous routes. Fields: trace_id, route, seq_len, model_variant, host_type, stage_times{tokenize, kv_lookup, batching_wait, model_fwd, postproc, egress}, cold_kv_flag, timestamp_ms
- Synthetic replay runs: 5 workloads (chat-short, chat-medium, completion-long, embeddings, rerank). Each replay ran for 30 minutes on a spare cluster to capture microburst behavior.
- Benchmarks: single-request microbenchmarks for model_fwd on GPU types A and B (median + tail from 100k in-process runs).

Instrumentation notes (gaps / gotchas):
- Batching_wait is reported as delta between 'batch_scheduled' and 'batch_started' in host-local time; some hosts have clock skew up to 5ms which inflates p50 slightly. We corrected by converting to monotonic deltas when possible.
- KV misses are flagged by cold_kv_flag but we only have presence, not miss_reason.
- Egress includes both encode time and network send; for dedicated hosts with local clients egress is <2ms, for hosted it can be 8–50ms depending on downlink.

Method: quantile stitching and per-stage attribution (high-level):
1) Partition traces into cohorts: route x model_variant x seq_len_bucket (0-64,65-256,>256) x host_type. This reduces confounding.
2) For each cohort, build empirical CDF of end-to-end latency and per-stage latencies.
3) To aggregate across cohorts with different traffic weight, compute traffic-weighted quantiles: sample N traces per cohort proportional to observed QPS (cap per cohort to avoid rare-cohort overdomination).
4) Compute p50/p95/p99 of end-to-end latency on the assembled sample.
5) Per-stage contribution to a given quantile: two complementary views:
   a) "Additive quantile attribution" (fast, approximate): compute per-stage median/95/99 and present stage share = stage_quantile / total_quantile. Useful for quick triage but can exceed 100% when stages overlap in tail.
   b) "Conditional slice decomposition" (more robust): for traces in the top X% (e.g., top 1% for p99), compute the distribution of stage times and report percent of traces where a stage >= 40% of trace. Also compute co-occurrence matrix for top-tier traces. This gives actionable signals (e.g., p99 dominated by batching_wait in 62% of top traces).
6) Cross-check with synthetic replays and kernel microbenchmarks to separate host-local model_fwd regressions from system-level batching/queueing effects.

Example results (first-pass numbers, approximate):
- Composite (traffic-weighted) latencies: p50 = 48ms, p95 = 215ms, p99 = 480ms
- Cohort examples (chat-medium, variant-v1, seqlen 65-256): p50=62ms p95=310ms p99=680ms

Per-stage quick-attribution (additive approx):
- Tokenize: p50=1ms p95=2ms p99=5ms (negligible)
- KV_lookup: p50=3ms p95=12ms p99=45ms (in p99 often cold misses)
- Batching_wait: p50=8ms p95=90ms p99=320ms (major tail contributor)
- Model_fwd: p50=28ms p95=70ms p99=90ms (tails grow with seqlen but not the dominant p99 for these cohorts)
- Postproc+egress: p50=4ms p95=18ms p99=30ms

Conditional slice decomposition (top 1% traces):
- 62% of top-1% traces have batching_wait >= 50% of total latency
- 21% of top-1% traces include cold_kv_flag == true and these traces have median extra +110ms
- Co-occurrence: when batching_wait high, model_fwd is rarely the largest fraction (only 14% of these cases) -> suggests queueing/scheduling vs model slowdown

Hypotheses generated from the above:
- Root cause for p99: rare large batching_delay spikes (scheduling jitter + contention for async worker slots) amplified by occasional cold KV misses.
- Model_fwd micro-regressions exist but contribute more to p95 than p99 in normal traffic mix.

Mitigation candidates (with rough impact estimate):
- Reduce max_batch_wait from 50ms -> 30ms for chat-medium routes: estimated p99 reduction ~30–45ms but increases p50 slightly for some throughput-critical bursts. (owner: Liam)
- Prewarm KV for hot prefixes during load spikes (heatmap-triggered prefetch): reduces cold_kv tail; estimated p99 improvement ~+80–120ms on affected cohort. (owner: Diego)
- Introduce a small prioritized fast-path queue for latency-sensitive routes to avoid head-of-line batching waits; prototype via adaptive queue knobs. Expected p99 wins for sensitive routes. (owner: Aisha)
- Investigate host scheduler jitter: instrument host-level worker wakeup histograms and kernel scheduling events during top traces. (owner: SRE)

Visualization recipe (for the dashboard / one-page slides):
- Top-left: composite CDF (log x-axis) p50/p95/p99 markers
- Top-right: stacked bar per-quantile showing additive-approx stage slices for p50/p95/p99
- Middle: cohort heatmap (rows=route, cols=quantiles) shading by p99 magnitude
- Bottom: conditional co-occurrence matrix for top-1% traces (percentages) + example trace timelines (3 exemplar traces annotated)

Open questions / follow-ups (in rough priority):
- How stable are the batching_wait spikes across days? Need rolling 7-day window sample comparison.
- Can we get richer KV diagnostics (miss reason, backend latency) without PII exposure? (product/security)
- Is there a correlation with autoscaling events / node churn? Add autoscaler event markers to traces.
- Validate synthetic replay representativeness for microburst shapes (saturday vs weekday differences).

Action items (short):
- [ ] Liam: change max_batch_wait on staged route and run 24h A/B (jira:SRV-3489)
- [ ] Diego: prototype prefix prewarm for top-100 hot prefixes during spike windows (PR: repo/cache-prefetch#6)
- [ ] SRE: add worker wakeup histogram to trace payload for a 48h window (link to infra ticket)
- [ ] Aisha: build dashboard mockup and attach 3 exemplar traces for review (confluence:trace-ensemble-dash)

Notes-to-self / style: keep the composite report conservative (use conditional decomposition for any claim of "dominant cause") and always show both additive and conditional views. Present expected impact ranges with uncertainties (low/med/high) and attach raw cohort counts so PMs understand sample sizes.

Appendix (quick reproducibility steps):
1) pull sampled traces: python tools/trace_export.py --start 2025-01-07 --end 2025-01-08 --routes chat-* --out traces.jsonl
2) run cohort assembler: python tools/cohort_assembler.py --in traces.jsonl --weight-by qps --cap 50k --out stitched_sample.jsonl
3) run quantile reporter: python tools/quantile_report.py --in stitched_sample.jsonl --cohorts meta.json --out report.yml
4) generate dashboard plot: tools/plot_maker --report report.yml --examples 3 --out report.pdf

If anything above looks off or someone wants raw numbers, ping and I will attach the trace slices and the synthetic run configs.

(end of draft)
